tagline: Write it once, send it everywhere, watch what lands.
intro: Blast turns your Bond CRM contacts into an audience for bulk email. You compose a message once, in a visual block editor, raw HTML, or from a saved template, pick who should receive it, and send. After every send, Blast records what happened to each recipient and rolls the results into per-campaign and org-wide analytics. This chapter walks you from a first draft through Send Now to reading opens, clicks, bounces, and unsubscribes, and it shows where an agent can assemble a campaign for your approval.
atAGlance: Three ways to build an email body: visual block editor, raw HTML, or a saved template
Segments that filter your Bond contacts and cache a contact count
Per-recipient delivery tracking plus per-campaign and org-wide analytics
Automatic open, click, bounce, complaint, and unsubscribe handling with no UI to wire
A CAN-SPAM gate that blocks any send missing an unsubscribe link or a physical address

pullQuotes.after: every send and engagement event is published
pullQuotes.text: Blast pulls its audience from Bond and pushes every send and engagement event into Bolt, so your automation can react the moment an email lands.

pullQuotes.after: resolve campaigns, templates, and segments by human-readable name
pullQuotes.text: Most agent tools resolve campaigns, templates, and segments by name, so an agent can act on the April Product Launch campaign without ever knowing its ID.

callouts.after: The simplest fix is to use the default template footer
callouts.text: The default template footer already includes an unsubscribe link, so the fastest way to clear the CAN-SPAM gate is to build on a template and just add your mailing address to the body.

callouts.after: deleting a campaign all exist in the API and MCP tools
callouts.text: The campaign detail page only renders Send Now today. Scheduling, pausing, cancelling, editing, and deleting a campaign all exist in the API and MCP tools, but you reach them through the API or a tool, not the detail UI.

callouts.after: Once an address unsubscribes (or files a spam complaint)
callouts.text: Unsubscribes are org-wide and keyed on the email address. Once an address unsubscribes or files a spam complaint, it is suppressed across the whole org and excluded from every future send. There is no per-campaign opt back in.

callouts.after: it schedules the campaign about an hour out and returns a note
callouts.text: Have an agent call blast_send_campaign with the default require_human_approval set to true, then open the campaigns list and watch it land as a scheduled campaign about an hour out, awaiting your confirmation before any mail leaves.

quiz.q: How many states can a campaign be in?
Which campaign status is the terminal success state and the only one analytics counts?
What two things must a campaign's HTML body contain to pass the CAN-SPAM gate?
quiz.answer: An unsubscribe mechanism (such as an {{unsubscribe_url}} merge field or text containing unsubscribe or opt-out) and a physical mailing address.
quiz.where: Key concepts: CAN-SPAM gate, and Why a send was rejected

quiz.q: Which two campaign statuses make the Send Now button appear on the detail page?
Where does Blast pull its audience from, and where does it push its send and engagement events?
quiz.answer: It pulls its audience from Bond (contacts and segments over Bond contact fields) and pushes activity into Bolt so automation rules can react.

quiz.q: Where is the platform SMTP relay actually configured?
choices: In the Bam app under Account Settings then Integrations
Per campaign on the create form
quiz.answer: In the Bam app under Account Settings then Integrations

quiz.q: What does blast_send_campaign do by default when require_human_approval is true?
quiz.answer: It does not send immediately; it schedules the campaign about an hour out and returns a note that a human must confirm before it goes.

quiz.q: How many rows does the Recipients table show per page on the campaign detail page?
What are the two match modes for joining a segment's conditions?
quiz.answer: ALL conditions (AND), which requires every condition, and ANY condition (OR), which matches any one.
quiz.where: Key concepts: Segment, and Segment builder and preview

quiz.q: What scope do you need to add or remove a sender domain?
When a spam complaint arrives, what three things does Blast do automatically?
quiz.answer: It marks the recipient complained, increments the complaints counter, and automatically unsubscribes that address org-wide.

quiz.q: What do the blast_draft_email_content and blast_suggest_subject_lines tools return?
choices: An error until a model is configured
The contents of a saved template
